title: Unblock queue promotion after stale active PRD
specification:
# Unblock queue promotion when a merged active PRD remains planned

## Observed symptom
The Moving Game queue is frozen after a merged PRD. On 2026-05-19T22:49:36Z, `GET /status?repoId=moving-game` still reported `pressure-ui-start-button-feedback` as a planned active PRD, `pm-agent` idle with `10 PRDs awaiting planning`, `architecture-agent` idle with no queued tasks, `reviewer` idle with no review tasks, and no active PM/implementation/review lane. Local queue files `prompts/autonomous/v2/queues/{pm-agent,architecture-agent,reviewer}.json` are empty.

## Evidence inspected
- Root `git status --short --branch`: clean `dev...origin/dev` at `390ce56`.
- Recent git history includes `cf1ff12 [reviewer-agent] merge [architecture-agent] Clarify matching game start button feedback`, matching the stale active PRD task.
- `.autonomy/control/dev-sync` was clean but stale at `9b82ac0`; the helper refreshed it with `git -C .autonomy/control/dev-sync fetch origin dev` and `git -C .autonomy/control/dev-sync reset --hard origin/dev`, after which it matched `390ce56`.
- After refresh, status still showed the same planned active PRD and idle lanes.
- Local active file `prompts/autonomous/v2/specs/prds/pressure-ui-start-button-feedback.json` exists.
- Local state file `prompts/autonomous/v2/specs/prd-state/pressure-ui-start-button-feedback.json` still says `status: planned`, `updatedAt: 2026-05-19T21:29:36.770Z`.
- Local queued PRD files remain present: `pressure-accessible-control-labels`, `pressure-score-readability`, `pressure-mobile-controls-polish`, `pressure-game-over-clarity`, `pressure-restart-flow-polish`, `pressure-loading-empty-state`, `pressure-reduced-motion-safety`, `pressure-layout-small-screen`, and `pressure-code-health-tiny-cleanup`.
- Duplicate check for this `autonomy-v2` PRD id returned `existingJobs: []`.
- A prior same-cause PRD was mistakenly added to `moving-game` as product queue state; this defect belongs to Autonomy infrastructure because it is scheduler/PRD reconciliation behavior.

## Likely root cause
The Autonomy scheduler/reconciler does not reliably complete/archive an active PRD after its implementation/review merge has landed, leaving queued PRDs unpromoted and normal worker queues empty. A pending deploy exists for Moving Game, but deploy feedback cannot unblock the next PRD while promotion is stuck behind stale active PRD state.

## Scope
Fix the Autonomy V2 queue/PRD reconciliation path that derives active PRD status from merged review/task evidence and promotes the next queued PRD. Start with the scheduler/reconciler code that reads repo-local `specs/prds`, `specs/prd-state`, review queues, and merged task records.

## Acceptance criteria
- A merged active PRD is no longer exposed as planned/active solely because its local `prd-state` file is stale.
- The reconciler archives or marks complete the merged active PRD, then promotes or queues PM planning for the next queued PRD.
- `/status?repoId=moving-game` no longer shows idle PM/implementation/reviewer lanes with queued PRDs and no queue work for this stale-active condition after reconciliation.
- The fix is implemented in `autonomy-v2`, not as a product UI change in `moving-game`.
- Validation includes a focused reconciliation/status test or equivalent local simulation for the stale-active merged PRD case, plus `npm run typecheck` in `autonomy-v2`.

## Validation
Run the smallest relevant Autonomy V2 reconciliation/status test for stale active PRD promotion and `npm run typecheck`. After release/consumption, re-check `GET /status?repoId=moving-game` and confirm one queued PRD is promoted or a PM planning task exists.
requirements: Repair Autonomy queue/PRD reconciliation so merged active PRDs do not block queued PRD promotion.
Keep the fix in autonomy-v2 infrastructure; do not change moving-game product UI behavior.

tasks.title: Repair stale active PRD reconciliation and queued PRD promotion
tasks.description: Fix the Autonomy V2 scheduler/reconciler path that derives active PRD state from repo-local PRD specs, PRD state files, implementation/review queues, merged task records, and git/GitHub evidence. A PRD whose implementation/review work has merged into the configured integration branch `dev` must not remain exposed as planned/active solely because `prompts/autonomous/v2/specs/prd-state/<prd>.json` is stale. After reconciling the completed active PRD, the system should archive or mark it complete using existing conventions and allow the next queued PRD to be promoted into the normal PM planning flow. Likely touch points include `src/sync/`, `src/autonomy-v2/commands/`, `src/autonomy-v2/control-plane/`, and scheduler/status code that reads `prompts/autonomous/v2/specs/prds`, `prompts/autonomous/v2/specs/prd-state`, `prompts/autonomous/v2/queues`, review queues, and merged task records.
acceptance: A focused stale-active fixture or simulation with an active PRD spec, stale `prd-state` value `planned`, evidence that the associated implementation/review work has merged into `dev`, empty PM/implementation/reviewer queues, and at least one queued PRD no longer reports the merged PRD as the sole planned active PRD after reconciliation.
The reconciliation path archives the merged active PRD or marks it complete using the repo's existing durable conventions, and it does so idempotently across repeated scheduler/status evaluations.

After the stale merged PRD is completed, the next queued PRD is promoted or PM planning is queued through the existing normal path; later queued PRDs are not skipped or duplicated in the same evaluation cycle.
Control-plane status for the stale-active condition no longer shows idle PM, implementation, and reviewer lanes while queued PRDs exist and no queue work is present.
The fix is implemented in `autonomy-v2` infrastructure code only and does not modify Moving Game product UI files or target `main`/`master` automation.
Verification includes a focused reconciliation/status unit test or equivalent local simulation for the stale active merged PRD case, plus `npm run typecheck`.
